title: Review correctness, reliability and measured limits

objectives.text: Evaluate a bounded revision-keyed evidence matrix with passed/failed/unverified states, stale evidence invalidation, duplicate rejection and explicit held gates.
Write a scoped release/learning review separating source correctness, integration, measured performance, operational readiness and competence/future-outcome claims.

blocks.markdown: A review should answer what was built, which revision/data/runtime was tested, how it was checked, what failed/was not checked, and what claims are supported. Authored means teaching exists; source-verified means stated source tests passed; fully signed needs actual applicable gates. A count of lessons or fixtures is not professional competence, cheating resistance, market realism or future-profit proof. Current model-risk guidance SR26-2 emphasizes scoped validation/limitations and supersedes SR11-7; it is not course accreditation.

Own matrix requires schema, math-reference, integration, mobile, accessibility, durable-recovery. Each record is (gate,revision,passed/failed/unverified). Missing or stale-revision evidence becomes unverified. Duplicate gate records are rejected instead of picking the favorable one. First three constitute this toy source_ready flag; all_listed_gates_passed means only this declared finite matrix, not universal production readiness. Reports themselves must be authenticated/inspected outside this bookkeeping function.

blocks.title: A previous mobile pass cannot sign a new revision

steps.text: For revisionr1,schema/math-reference/integrationpassed. Mobilepassed only for oldrevision, so r1mobileis unverified. Accessibility/durable-recoverymissing also unverified.
source_ready True, all_listed_gates_passed False; held mobile/accessibility/durable-recovery. For new r2, all earlier r1 source evidence is stale too, so source_ready False.

Duplicate evidence gate is an error, not proof of two independent reviews. A failed record remains failed rather than relabeled planned or silently omitted. Final presentation must preserve evidence scope and unresolved gates.

blocks.caption: Expected True False; (mobile,accessibility,durable-recovery); False; invalid duplicate or unknown evidence. Tuple output quotes gate names. Complete pure bookkeeping source, no test execution/artifact signature/identity check. Required matrix is own educational example, not exhaustive platform/security/regulatory readiness or professional certification.

blocks.markdown: Use independent mathematical/reference algorithms, property/metamorphic/domain/error cases and actual source execution, with tolerances/runtime/capabilities declared. Roundtrip/shared-kernel checks can share a bug. Structural types/validator fixtures show contract consistency, not teaching quality or every algorithm correct. Editorial review must read teaching/objective/assessment alignment, worked examples and source caveats. Hidden test passes can support evaluation evidence without proving no cheating or job competence.

Report workload, hardware/runtime/build flags, measurement protocol, queue/arrival model, warmup/repetitions and units/distribution before making speed/latency claims. A tiny local deterministic run is not production scale; mean alone hides tails and completed-only sampling can hide timeouts. Recovery exceptions are not power-loss/concurrent tests. List exactly which actual user flows/storage/mobile/a11y/security/operational gates remain, and avoid deleting functionality to make the label green.

A useful limits section says unsupported models/domains/currencies, unverified capabilities, source/data assumptions, known failures and evidence that would change the assessment. No-data is not pass. A planned check is not an authored/verified check; an archived source is not actual deployed state. Preserve old checkpoint and revision provenance so regressions can be traced and rolled back under tested compatibility/authority. This review performs no deployment or account change.

Objective-level checks assess demonstrated skills under their grading contract, with reflection not-assessed/self-review rather than fake semantic grading. Mastery/practice links require genuine main teaching evidence, not only a matching concept ID or a prerequisite mention. Independent transfer tasks and broader project/review evidence help learning, but no fixed completion count guarantees future work competence. The earlier five foundation practice-teaching gaps (base conversion, fixed-point permutations, bounded walks, expected maximum of dice and modular coupon collection) now have reviewed Python main teaching for their supplied-parser contracts. That bounded teaching fit does not establish C++ execution, remote judge qualification, operational readiness or professional competence. Check the current revision-bound evidence for each separate claim rather than retaining a stale gap count.

Independent transfer: produce a revision-scoped review from an actual artifact with evidence references, failed/unverified gates and supported claims. Change revision and invalidate stale records; inject duplicate and failed evidence. Design one independent reference and one actual mobile/recovery test the source suite cannot replace. Keep professional competence, production compliance and future returns outside the completion claim unless separately established.

Sources: [current SR26-2 scoped validation/limitations](https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.pdf), [Google SRE monitoring/measurement context](https://sre.google/workbook/monitoring/), [canary/release evidence](https://sre.google/workbook/canarying-releases/), [OWASP authorization/security scope](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html). Own gate matrix and curriculum evidence labels are not external certification standards.

summary: Review exact revision-bound evidence and preserve failed/unverified gates. Source, teaching, integration, measurement and actual operational/app checks are different claims. All listed toy gates passing is not universal readiness, professional competence or future-outcome proof.
